one_line: AI-native trip planner turns saved Instagram Reels into routed itineraries.
what_it_does: Ingests Reel links, extracts and verifies places, checks routes/weather, groups stops into days, and lets a user edit the live map through an agent.
leverage_rationale: Structured in-page tools let the agent operate on saved reels, itinerary state, and map edits with shared state rather than fragile multi-tab UI driving; the same outcome is possible manually but substantially less reliably.
leverage_evidence: Pitch says WebMCP tools run inside the page and save pasted Reel links/start extraction.
About text describes visible add_place calls, recalled preferences, verification, routing, and reporting missing forecast rather than fabricating it.
execution_rationale: The described central workflow is coherent and appears substantially implemented, but the packet has no transcript and image review was unavailable, so end-to-end completion is claimed rather than observed.
execution_evidence: Demo is marked alive and public repository exists.
About text describes staged extraction, verification, approval, routing, and adding a user-owned stop.
impact_rationale: Targets a concrete travel-planning pain point for people with inspiration saved in social media and converts it into an actionable itinerary.
impact_evidence: About text identifies the gap between saved Reels and usable trip plans.
Itinerary includes routes, geography-based days, and weather/verification handling.
creativity_rationale: The social-video-to-live-3D-trip-planning concept is a fresh, memorable synthesis with a meaningful conversational editing model.
creativity_evidence: Combines Instagram Reel inspiration, multi-agent extraction, verification, and live 3D mapping.
Agent-added stops are explicitly distinguished from Reel-derived places.
usability_note: Conversational control addresses reported navigation confusion, though the long processing time may affect usability.
red_flags: No submitted video or transcript; visual claims could not be independently checked.
standouts: Strong bridge from saved social content to an actual route.
advance_reason: Strong concept and meaningful WebMCP-centered workflow, with enough claimed implementation to merit advancement despite thin visual evidence.

one_line: A live Shark Tank-style arena where AI investors challenge founders in real time.
what_it_does: Stages competitive founder pitches with four AI investor personalities, using WebMCP to let an agent control and participate in the arena experience.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP provides structured control of a live theatrical game state and lets a visiting AI participate, but a general agent could likely reproduce much of the interaction with UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly describes four AI investors challenging founders in real time through WebMCP.
About text frames the website itself as exposing the game to visiting AI.
execution_rationale: The concept and history are coherent, but packet evidence is mostly narrative and lacks a video transcript or gallery imagery; functional completeness is therefore uncertain.
execution_evidence: Demo is marked alive and repository is public.
About text describes an existing pitch arena brought back as a WebMCP experience.
impact_rationale: Offers clear entertainment and experimentation value for founders and people curious about multi-agent interaction, though the practical audience/problem fit is narrower.
impact_evidence: Shark Tank-style competition and shareable results are stated goals.
Project is presented as a live challenge experience rather than a generic chatbot.
creativity_rationale: A multi-investor AI pitch theater is a notably original interaction model and uses personality, competition, and performance rather than a routine productivity task.
creativity_evidence: Four AI investors challenge founders in real time.
Concept combines human pitching, agent participation, and game-like governance.
usability_note: Live arena framing is understandable, but no visual evidence was available to assess flow.
red_flags: About text says Pitch The AI existed before the challenge and was previously a side experience.
No video transcript or gallery imagery.
standouts: Memorable theatrical framing for human-agent collaboration.
advance_reason: Creative concept, but WebMCP delta, current execution, and challenge eligibility are insufficiently evidenced; stated pre-challenge history is a material concern.

one_line: Recovery contracts let agents resume failed multi-step workflows without repeating valid work.
what_it_does: Journals workflow steps, classifies preserved/recovered/blocked actions, searches alternatives, requests human approval, and selectively resumes onboarding after partial failure.
leverage_rationale: Shared structured recovery state and selective-resume tools address a failure mode that ordinary UI-driving agents handle unreliably; WebMCP is central to the product's safety contract.
leverage_evidence: Six tools expose onboarding state, recovery plan, alternative slots, proposal, and resume.
Demo explicitly preserves four successful actions and avoids replaying them after the fifth fails.
Human approval remains in the webpage with deliberately no approval tool.
execution_rationale: The scope is tightly defined and the claimed workflow, failure state, recovery proposal, approval boundary, and resume behavior form a coherent complete demo; visual observation was unavailable.
execution_evidence: Deterministic simulated services make the partial failure reproducible.
IndexedDB persistence, append-only journaling, idempotency, and selective resume are specified.
Demo is alive and repository is public.
impact_rationale: Partial failure and unsafe retries are a serious, general problem in agent automation; preserving valid side effects while requiring approval for irreversible actions has direct safety value.
impact_evidence: Concrete employee-onboarding scenario demonstrates four preserved actions and one recovered action.
Irreversible welcome email stays blocked until human approval.
creativity_rationale: The recovery-contract framing and preserved/recovered/blocked state model are an original, technically ambitious answer to a neglected agent reliability problem.
creativity_evidence: Application-declared recovery semantics plus selective resume.
Separates recovery inspection/proposal from human approval.
usability_note: Explicit recovery states and approval boundary should make failure handling legible; simulated services limit real-world validation.
red_flags: No transcript and visual evidence unavailable; runtime behavior remains claimed.
standouts: Exceptionally clear failure/recovery contract and non-replay guarantee.
advance_reason: High WebMCP leverage and impact with a focused, safety-relevant workflow that is unusually well specified.

one_line: A live GitHub task board coordinates agents from claim through reviewed pull request.
what_it_does: Lets humans create tasks and agents inspect, claim, plan, execute, link PRs, read review state, and check CI while maintaining ownership and shared workflow state.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes changing, context-bounded tools over shared live ticket state, with atomic first-claim ownership and human takeover controls; general UI automation cannot match the reliability of this coordination contract.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes ticket-specific tools, shared revision state over WebSockets, and atomic claim prevention.
Transcript demonstrates claim, plan, implementation, PR, review feedback, fix, merge, and done transitions.
Separate worktrees isolate concurrent tasks while ownership remains visible.
execution_rationale: The 77-second demo transcript covers the central workflow end to end across multiple agent threads, including review and merge; only minor implementation edges are unverified.
execution_evidence: Video is 77 seconds with a full transcript.
Transcript explicitly describes claim through merge and ticket status transitions.
Public repository and live demo metadata are provided.
impact_rationale: Directly addresses real coordination failures in teams using coding agents: collisions, stale ownership, detached plans, and opaque progress.
impact_evidence: About text identifies concrete failure modes and human authority boundaries.
Workflow maps naturally to GitHub PR review and CI.
creativity_rationale: The shared agent task board is a strong, ambitious synthesis of issue tracking, agent permissions, live state, and PR lifecycle rather than a simple agent wrapper.
creativity_evidence: Tools change with ticket/workflow/current assignment.
Signed-in user plus per-tab capability and explicit human takeover are notable interaction details.
usability_note: Explicit columns, ownership, and PR states create a legible team workflow; login is a setup requirement.
standouts: Best evidence packet: transcript demonstrates multi-agent lifecycle end to end.
Atomic ownership and human-controlled takeover are strong safety details.
advance_reason: Transformative WebMCP coordination with strong end-to-end video evidence and clear real-world impact.

one_line: An AI-assisted social publishing workspace for platform-specific previews and scheduling.
what_it_does: Creates, validates, previews, edits, publishes, and schedules variants across 11 social platforms through an assistant, web UI, SDK, API, or CLI.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP links the assistant to the same drafts and visual previews the person edits, improving structured multi-platform revision, but publishing is also exposed through several non-WebMCP interfaces.
leverage_evidence: WebMCP tools read drafts, render platform versions, edit previews, configure profiles, and bring previews into view.
Preview requires no signup or connected social account according to the packet.
execution_rationale: Broad capability and a coherent preview/edit/publish story are described, but no video or transcript is supplied and the repository is not public, limiting verification.
execution_evidence: Demo is marked alive and gallery_images=3.
About text lists 11 platforms plus scheduler, SDK, HTTP API, and CLI.
impact_rationale: Serves creators and social teams with a concrete repetitive workflow: adapting one idea, media, and thread structure across networks and scheduling it.
impact_evidence: About text identifies copying, per-network adjustment, media upload, and separate scheduling as the problem.
Platform-specific previews and editing directly address that friction.
creativity_rationale: Useful and well-integrated, but social publishing and cross-platform scheduling are established categories; the shared AI/preview workspace is the main new angle.
creativity_evidence: Agent and human edit the same underlying content with platform-specific variants.
Supports assistant, UI, SDK, API, and CLI surfaces.
usability_note: Preview-first editing and no-signup access are favorable; breadth across 11 platforms may add complexity.
red_flags: No public repository and no video transcript; publishing integrations are not independently demonstrated.
standouts: Strong same-content/shared-preview model between person and assistant.
advance_reason: Credible audience and useful shared workspace, though the WebMCP delta and execution are less strongly evidenced than the leading infrastructure projects.

one_line: An SVG design editor exposes its full canvas toolset to outside AI agents.
what_it_does: Lets agents create and revise flyers, social graphics, templates, gradients, icons, layouts, and dynamic fields on the same live SVG canvas used by a person.
leverage_rationale: Exposing structured editor operations and shared live canvas state makes iterative agent-directed design materially more precise than returning raw SVG or one-shot images, though a capable agent could drive some UI manually.
leverage_evidence: About text states around 100 editor tools are exposed, with 48 curated tools and meta-tools for the remainder.
set_agent_identity, lock_canvas, ask_canvas_question, and shared canvas coordination are described.
Agent can draw, align, template, and map dynamic fields using the same editor tools.
execution_rationale: The editor scope and agent/human coordination model are detailed and internally coherent, with live demo and gallery evidence claimed; no visual inspection was possible.
execution_evidence: Demo alive, public repository, and two gallery images are listed.
Detailed tool architecture and curated registration strategy are provided.
Workflow includes lock, question, editing, and human takeover.
impact_rationale: Addresses a real gap for people who want agents to produce editable, revisable graphics rather than opaque generated images or code snippets.
impact_evidence: About text contrasts raw SVG/one-shot output with a real revisable design tool.
Targets flyers, social posts, promos, and reusable templates.
creativity_rationale: Agent collaboration inside a full visual editor, including identity, canvas locking, questions, and reusable schema-backed templates, is a fresh and ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Approximately 100 editor operations exposed to arbitrary outside agents.
Human can watch and take over on the shared canvas.
usability_note: Shared canvas and explicit locking support collaboration, but a very large tool surface could be difficult for agents and users to navigate.
red_flags: No transcript; image evidence could not be independently checked.
standouts: Strongly treats the agent as a participant in a real design editor, not an image-output endpoint.
advance_reason: High-quality WebMCP/editor integration with clear creative and practical value.

one_line: A WebMCP electronics shop helps agents assemble compatible fictional PCs.
what_it_does: Provides catalog browsing, filtering, product details, variation selection, and a build summary where an agent reasons about component compatibility without placing real orders.
leverage_rationale: Structured product and build-state tools let agents connect compatibility constraints more reliably than reading long spec pages, but the underlying shopping outcome remains achievable with ordinary browsing.
leverage_evidence: Packet states 15 WebMCP tool descriptors and same-tab operation.
About text emphasizes connecting component details and explaining compatibility.
User retains decisions such as cart additions and watchdog creation.
execution_rationale: The fictional shop has a coherent browse-to-build scope and live demo with four gallery images, but there is no video or public repository to verify behavior.
execution_evidence: Demo marked alive and gallery_images=4.
Product catalog, detail, and build summary surfaces are specified.
Made-up data is explicitly disclosed.
impact_rationale: PC builders and less technical shoppers have a real compatibility/research problem, and an agent that explains component interactions can reduce costly mistakes even in a demo setting.
impact_evidence: Inspiration describes incompatible GPU/case and fragmented spec research.
Product's stated focus is compatibility explanation rather than silent purchasing.
creativity_rationale: Agent-assisted PC compatibility shopping is a competent, useful take on a known commerce problem, with the shared same-tab build state as its fresh angle.
creativity_evidence: Agent connects multiple component categories in a floating build summary.
Human control is retained for cart and watchdog decisions.
usability_note: A build summary and guided compatibility reasoning should help novices; fictional catalog limits real shopping utility.
red_flags: All catalog, prices, stock, reviews, and performance data are fictional.
No video transcript or public repository.
standouts: Clear same-tab compatibility reasoning with explicit human control.
advance_reason: Solid demo concept, but impact is constrained by fictional data and evidence is too thin to outrank stronger packets.

one_line: A shared shopping-mission board lets agents assemble multi-store kits while people lock or reject choices.
what_it_does: Parses a mission and budget, plans kit slots, searches Shopify catalogs across merchants, ranks candidates, incorporates human edits, and builds merchant checkout links.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP creates a shared, staged, stateful planning surface where agent and person co-edit constraints and selections; the agent reads human locks/rejections and replans rather than restarting, a major reliability delta over ordinary shopping UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Transcript demonstrates staged tool disclosure, tool-change events, shared edits, locked and rejected picks, and re-planning under budget.
Every tool result carries edits back to the agent and header shows the agent has seen them.
One board coordinates multiple merchants and checkout links.
execution_rationale: The 175-second transcript covers mission creation, planning, parallel search, kit completion, human decisions, replanning, budget preservation, and checkout-link generation in a coherent flow.
execution_evidence: Video is 175 seconds with a detailed transcript.
Transcript states a $373.17 kit across seven merchants and maintains budget after replacement.
Demo includes a real cart per merchant while leaving purchase to the user.
impact_rationale: Addresses a concrete cross-store planning problem for shoppers with budgets and constraints, preserving user preferences while reducing search and comparison work.
impact_evidence: Backpacking, car camping, espresso setup, and first-apartment examples establish multiple audiences.
Agent searches across stores while user controls trusted picks and purchases.
creativity_rationale: The shared mission board, staged tool surface, multi-merchant search, and human lock/reject/replan loop are a memorable and ambitious commerce interaction.
creativity_evidence: Agent and person jointly maintain a kit rather than the agent acting as a spectator or replacing choices.
Tool disclosure changes with context and edits are credited to their author.
usability_note: Mission cards, author attribution, budget tracking, and explicit checkout handoff support trust; multi-store checkout remains inherently complex.
red_flags: Transcript has a likely naming slip ('School Aura') and domain spelling inconsistency, but the workflow remains coherent.
standouts: Excellent evidence of genuine human-agent co-editing and replanning.
advance_reason: One of the strongest packets: transformative shared-state leverage, end-to-end evidence, clear audience value, and an original interaction model.

one_line: A Stanford academic-planning workspace where student and agent plan courses, goals, clubs, and progress together.
what_it_does: Maintains quarterly plans, course sections, AP credit, schedules, clubs, todos, milestones, notes, and activity attribution with agent-assisted catalog research.
leverage_rationale: Structured shared academic state lets an agent reason across course sections, schedules, clubs, goals, and user corrections in one workspace; ordinary browsing would be markedly more fragmented.
leverage_evidence: About text describes agent-selected sections around rehearsals/work-study and corrections visible to both parties.
Activity log attributes changes to student or agent across planning surfaces.
Agent searches the full course catalog and works with milestones and calendar state.
execution_rationale: The product scope is coherent and richly described with eight gallery images and a public repository, but no video/transcript and demo status is unknown, so completion is claimed.
execution_evidence: Eight gallery images are listed and public repository exists.
About text enumerates landing, week view, academics, clubs, scratchpad, and activity log surfaces.
Real course sections and discussions are claimed.
impact_rationale: Students facing complex schedules and long-term degree planning have a specific need for integrated, personalized planning and progress tracking.
impact_evidence: Stanford student scenario combines classes, AP credit, clubs, work-study, and rehearsals.
The stated problem is unreliable fragmented browsing and loss of personal context.
creativity_rationale: Academic planning is an established category, but the integrated student-agent workspace with attributed edits and calendar-aware course selection is a fresh synthesis.
creativity_evidence: Agent and student share corrections, activity provenance, goals, milestones, and schedule constraints.
Plans span every quarter through graduation.
usability_note: Multiple dedicated views and attribution support planning, though the breadth could create onboarding complexity.
red_flags: Demo status is unknown and no video transcript was provided.
Stanford-specific scope narrows applicability, but category neutrality means this is not a penalty.
standouts: Strong personal-context and provenance model across academics and life scheduling.
advance_reason: Clear audience need and compelling shared planning model, with enough packaging evidence to advance despite absent video.

one_line: A visual skill-tree canvas helps career switchers build learning roadmaps with an agent.
what_it_does: Turns agent-generated career-learning guidance into an interactive canvas of skill nodes and relationships, with tools exposed through native WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP can place and update structured roadmap nodes in a shared visual canvas, but the packet does not show enough to establish a large reliability or capability delta over an agent generating a roadmap and driving a canvas UI.
leverage_evidence: Pitch identifies an interactive skill tree integrated with native WebMCP.
About text describes dynamic skill nodes and console testing of tools.
execution_rationale: The concept is understandable, but no frame sheets were submitted and the about text is sparse/fragmented; the central workflow and completeness cannot be established.
execution_evidence: Demo is marked alive and four gallery images are listed.
Packet provides no submitted video frame sheets and no transcript.
About text claims canvas, interpretation, and console testing but does not evidence an end-to-end roadmap flow.
impact_rationale: Career switchers are a real audience facing confusing learning choices, and a visual roadmap can be more actionable than plain-text advice.
impact_evidence: Inspiration identifies job displacement and technology-choice confusion.
Product directly targets visualizing what to learn.
creativity_rationale: Visualizing agent explanations as a skill tree is a useful new angle on career guidance, but the packet does not establish deep or unusually ambitious pursuit.
creativity_evidence: Interactive skill nodes replace plain-text pathways.
Project proposes extending the canvas visualization model beyond careers.
usability_note: A visual tree may improve comprehension, but the sparse evidence leaves navigation and editing usability unclear.
red_flags: No video frame sheets submitted; visual claims cannot be checked.
Sparse, malformed-looking about text limits confidence.
standouts: Directly addresses the gap between text answers and visual learning plans.
advance_reason: Potentially useful concept, but execution and WebMCP behavior are too thinly evidenced for advancement.
